competencies.text: Explain how life forms operate as systems of related parts. Create a diagram showing structure-function relationships in biological systems.

days.title: Life as Interconnected Systems
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to explain the unifying themes of life science, describe how living things operate as systems of related parts, and relate structure to function in biological systems.

🌱 What Is Life Science?

Life science (biology) is the study of living things — from microscopic bacteria to giant whales. Despite the enormous diversity of life, all living things share certain unifying themes.

🔗 The Unifying Themes of Life

ThemeMeaningExample
1. Cell theoryAll living things are made of cells — the basic unit of lifeBacteria (one cell) to humans (trillions of cells)
2. Structure and functionThe shape of a part determines what it can doRed blood cells are disc-shaped to carry oxygen
3. Systems of related partsParts work together in organized systemsHeart + blood vessels + lungs = circulatory system
4. HomeostasisLiving things maintain a stable internal environmentSweating to cool down; shivering to warm up
5. Energy flowAll life needs energy — from the sun, food, or chemicalsPlants capture sunlight; animals eat plants
6. Reproduction & heredityLiving things pass information to the next generationDNA carries genetic code
7. EvolutionPopulations change over generationsAntibiotic-resistant bacteria
8. InterdependenceOrganisms depend on each other and their environmentBees pollinate flowers; plants give bees nectar

⚙️ Levels of Biological Organization

Life is organized in a hierarchy of levels — each level built from the one below:

Atom → Molecule → Cell → Tissue → Organ → Organ System → Organism → Population → Community → Ecosystem → Biosphere

LevelDefinitionExample
CellBasic unit of lifeRed blood cell, neuron
TissueGroup of similar cells doing the same jobMuscle tissue, blood
OrganGroup of tissues working togetherHeart, leaf, kidney
Organ systemGroup of organs working togetherCirculatory, digestive, respiratory systems
OrganismA complete living thingA human, a tree, a fish
PopulationSame species living in one areaCarabao in a field
CommunityDifferent species interactingRice field ecosystem (rice, insects, frogs, birds)
EcosystemCommunity + non-living environmentMangrove forest + water + soil
BiosphereAll life on EarthThe whole planet

🔬 Structure ↔ Function Relationship

In biology, structure determines function. Every part of a living thing has a shape or design that helps it do a specific job:

StructureFunction (What It Does)How Structure Helps
🌿 Leaf (flat, thin, wide)Capture sunlight for photosynthesisLarge surface area for absorbing light
🫁 Alveoli (tiny air sacs in lungs)Exchange oxygen and CO₂ with bloodMillions of tiny sacs = huge surface area
🩸 Red blood cell (disc-shaped, no nucleus)Carry oxygenBiconcave shape holds more hemoglobin; no nucleus frees space
🌳 Tree roots (branching)Absorb water and anchor the plantWidespread network reaches more soil
🐟 Fish gills (thin filaments)Extract oxygen from waterThin, rich in blood vessels for gas exchange
🦴 Bones (hollow tubes)Support body and protect organsHollow design = strong but light

🌏 Why This Matters

Understanding these themes helps us:

  • See connections between all life forms.
  • Predict how organisms respond to changes in their environment.
  • Understand medicine, agriculture, and conservation.
  • Appreciate why every part of an ecosystem matters.

📌 Quick Check

  • What is the basic unit of life? (Answer: the cell)
  • Why is a leaf flat and wide? (Answer: to maximize surface area for capturing sunlight)
  • What is homeostasis? (Answer: maintaining a stable internal environment)

days.title: Match Game — Structure & Function
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each structure to its function, or each theme to its correct meaning. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: All living things are made of cells
Maintaining a stable internal environment — like sweating to cool down
The shape of a part determines what it can do
Large surface area for capturing sunlight
Biconcave shape holds more oxygen-carrying hemoglobin
Huge surface area for gas exchange in the lungs
Organisms rely on each other — bees pollinate flowers

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Systems Thinking
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🫁 A person has emphysema — a disease that damages the alveoli in their lungs. Why does this make it hard to breathe?

choices.label: A) The lungs become too small
B) Damaged alveoli reduce the surface area for gas exchange, so less oxygen enters the blood
D) The person produces too much oxygen

scenario.text: 🌿 A plant is placed in a very dark room for a week. What happens and why?

choices.label: A) It grows faster because it doesn't need light
B) It wilts and yellows because photosynthesis (which needs light) cannot proceed
C) It stops growing roots but keeps growing leaves

scenario.text: 🩸 Why is a red blood cell's shape (a biconcave disc) important?

choices.label: A) The shape lets it hold more hemoglobin and squeeze through narrow capillaries
B) The shape makes it heavier so it stays in the blood
C) The shape helps it make antibodies
D) The shape is random — no function

scenario.text: 🐝 Bees collect nectar from flowers and transfer pollen. This is an example of:

choices.label: A) Interdependence — both species benefit from the relationship

scenario.text: 🥵 You go for a run under the hot sun and start to sweat. This is your body:

choices.label: B) Maintaining homeostasis by cooling itself

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Systems Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Systems Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: What is the basic unit of life?
Which of the following levels of biological organization is the MOST complex?
Which theme of life science explains why you sweat when it's hot?
Why are alveoli in the lungs so tiny and numerous?

choices.label: A) To create a huge surface area for gas exchange
B) To make them easier to see

escape.text: Which statement BEST describes the structure-function relationship?

choices.label: A) The shape of a biological part determines what job it can perform
B) All structures look the same
C) Function is random and unrelated to structure
D) Only animals have structure-function relationships

escape.text: Bees pollinating flowers while collecting nectar is an example of:
